senses.gloss:
दिधक्ष् दिधक्ष्, क्, क्, क् (fr. the Desid. of
rt. 1. दह्), wishing or intending to burn.
दिधक्षमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, wishing to burn.
दिधक्षयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, desiring to burn.

दिधक्षा, f. desire or wish to burn or consume
by fire.

दिधक्षु, उस्, उस्, उ, intending to burn or
destroy, desirous of burning.

दिधि दिधि, इस्, f. (fr. rt. 1. धा), firmness,
stability, fixed state of mind or being; (probably a
wrong form.)

दीधी 1. दीधी (connected with rt. 2.
दी), cl. 2. A. दीधीते (3rd pl. दीध्यते),
&c., Caus. दीधयति, &c., to shine, to be bright, to
seem, appear.

दीधी 2. दीधी (a reduplicated form of
1. धी and connected with rt. ध्यै),
cl. 2. A. दीधीते, &c., to perceive, think, reflect upon,
be intent upon; wish, desire.

दिधिक्ष् दिधिक्ष्, क्, क्, क् (fr. the Desid. of
rt. 1. दिह्), intending to smear.

दिधिषाय्य दिधिषाय्य, अस्, m. (fr. the
Desid. of rt. 1. धा), ‘to be tried to be gained,’ an
epithet of Agni; (Sāy.) a supporter; (अस्), m. a
pretended friend (?); [cf. दधिषाय्य, which is
by some considered as another reading.]

दिधिषु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. wishing or trying to
gain or obtain; (उस्), m. a suitor; a husband; the
second husband of a woman twice married; (उस् or
दिधिषू, ऊस्), f. a virgin widow remarried; an
elder sister unmarried having a younger married
sister; [cf. अग्रे-द्˚ and एदिधिषुः-पति.]
—दि-
धिषू-पति, इस्, m. the husband of a woman re-
married.

1. दीधिति, इस्, f. brightness, splendor, light; a
ray [cf. अमृत-द्˚]; a finger, (connected by Vedic
commentators with rt. 1. धा or 3. धी); N. of
a commentary on the Tattva-cintā-maṇi by Śiro-
maṇi treating of the Nyāya doctrines.
—दीधिति-
मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having splendor, shining, brilliant;
(आन्), m. the sun.

2. दीधिति, इस्, f., Ved. religious reflection, devo-
tion; divine inspiration; prayer; religious rites;
(Sāy.) a son-in-law (= धर्तृ, जामातृ, connected
with 1. धा).
दीध्यान, अस्, आ, अम्, shining, brilliant.
